countries.name: India
countries.summary: India's higher-education system is overseen by the Ministry of Education and its statutory regulators - the University Grants Commission for universities and degrees, the All India Council for Technical Education for technical and management programmes, and the National Medical Commission for medical education. International applicants normally enter through an institution's own international-admissions office, through the government's Study in India portal, or through a centrally administered scheme such as DASA for engineering and architecture seats at NITs, IIITs and other centrally funded technical institutes. Entry rules differ by nationality, residency status, the prior qualification held and the discipline chosen.
countries.whyStudentsChooseIt: International applicants look at India for English-taught degrees across computing, engineering, management, design, sciences, law and health disciplines, and for a single national application route: the Ministry of Education's Study in India portal issues an SII ID and lets an applicant send one profile to several participating institutes. Government-funded study places also exist through Indian Council for Cultural Relations scholarship schemes, which are applied for through Indian diplomatic missions rather than directly to a university. What an individual applicant can access depends on citizenship, residency status, how the prior qualification is assessed for equivalence, and whether the programme is attached to a national entrance test.
countries.climate: Climate varies widely by region, from alpine Himalayan conditions in the north to tropical coastal and semi-arid zones further south, with a June-to-September monsoon across most of the country.

universities.name: O.P. Jindal Global University
universities.summary: O.P. Jindal Global University is a private university at Sonipat in Haryana, founded in 2009 and listed by the University Grants Commission among Haryana's private universities. Its twelve schools teach law, business, international affairs, public policy, liberal arts, psychology and public health in English on a fully residential campus of more than 16,000 students.
universities.campusLifestyle: JGU is fully residential, with more than 16,000 students, over 1,100 full-time faculty and around 2,900 administrative staff on one campus at Sonipat Narela Road. Faculty come from more than 50 countries and students from more than 75. The Global Library covers 15,000 square feet, seats over 650 people at once, and keeps more than 60 per cent of its floor area open around the clock. Named facilities include the Naveen Jindal Sports Academy, the RASA and SAMA student activity spaces, a Film and Television Studio and Multimedia Lab, and 50 bookable conference and breakout rooms.
universities.cityProfile: The campus sits on Sonipat Narela Road near Jagdishpur village, in a Haryana district that borders Delhi and Uttar Pradesh and is bounded on the east by the Yamuna. Sonipat district covers 2,260 square kilometres and adjoins Rohtak, Jind and Panipat. The original Grand Trunk Road ran through what is now the campus, and a kos minar milestone from the era of Sher Shah Suri and Jehangir still stands near a campus gate beside the student housing block. The wider region carries deep archaeological significance: Rakhigarhi, in Haryana's Hisar district, is the largest known Harappan excavation. Sonipat also has an unusually dense sporting record, sending more Olympians to the 2021 Tokyo Games than any other Indian district. For an international student this is small-town Haryana rather than metropolitan Delhi, which shapes what is available off campus.
universities.practicalExposure: Applied work is built into each of these degrees rather than offered as an extra. The B.A. (Hons.) Liberal Arts and Humanities requires five internships, mixed academic and corporate, across the four years. The M.A. Public Policy carries a mandatory two-credit internship, with an optional six-month capstone project for students who want longer applied work. The Master of Public Health combines an internship with a dissertation, capstone project or community service learning project. The two-year MBA places internships in the summer and winter vacations. Support comes from the Office of Career Services and the Office of Career and Professional Development, which run career counselling, resume and cover letter workshops, interview skills training, networking events and placement assistance. Jindal Global Business School lists recruiters including Deloitte, KPMG, PwC, Accenture, ICICI Bank, American Express, Rolls-Royce, Tata Consultancy Services, Wipro, HCL and Infosys, and internship hosts including Tata Motors, Tech Mahindra, Reliance Retail, CRY (Child Rights and You) and the SRF Foundation. The Jindal School of Government and Public Policy names UNDP, the World Health Organisation in Geneva, NITI Aayog, the Centre for Policy Research, Observer Research Foundation, Pratham and Teach for India among the destinations of its public policy alumni. The five-year law degrees add four compulsory clinical courses and five compulsory internships, at least one of them under Trial and Appellate Advocates; Jindal Global Law School opens recruitment with a Zero Day Placement Event in the penultimate year, and around 40 to 50 organisations engage with its Office of Career Services each hiring cycle.
universities.hostelOverview: JGU is a fully residential university and publishes accommodation charges alongside tuition for each residential programme. Rooms are shared: the Student Handbook states accommodation is on a three- and four-people sharing basis, with no single occupancy available. For 2026-27 the annual residential charge is INR 2,32,000 on the five-year law degrees, INR 2,31,100 on the liberal arts, political science and MBA programmes and INR 1,81,100 on the M.A. Public Policy. Allied service charges covering food, laundry, security, housekeeping and electricity add INR 1,48,900 a year on the law degrees and INR 1,24,900 elsewhere, and a one-time refundable deposit of INR 50,000 applies. Both charges rise by up to ten per cent a year. The Master of Public Health is non-residential and carries neither.
universities.dietarySupport: Catering and housekeeping are contracted to Sodexo. All JGU dining halls serve vegetarian food, with eggs in some meals; non-vegetarian food is available on payment at other campus outlets. The Vidya Devi Jindal dining block runs over seven floors and seats 7,000 at a time. Named outlets in the T6 food court include Subway, Bikanervala, Dunkin', Oki Poki and Millets & More, most open from 11:00 to 01:00. Dining staff handle allergy, intolerance and religious dietary requests on request.
universities.safetyOverview: The JGU Health Centre has a dedicated Emergency Ward and runs a 24/7 helpline staffed by a resident medical officer on duty, backed by an Emergency Response Coordination Centre and Advanced Cardiac Life Support and Basic Life Support ambulances stationed across campus. A published escalation matrix runs from the duty officer through the head of nursing to the Chief Medical Superintendent. Security issues route to a Quick Response Team.
universities.studentSupport: Sukoon On Campus provides 24x7 mental health support, confidential one-to-one therapy and a dedicated helpline. Statutory bodies include the Anti-Ragging Committee, the Committee on Gender Sensitisation Against Sexual Harassment, the Committee on Disability Issues and the Anti-Discrimination Committee. The English Language Centre, running since 2012, teaches reading, writing, listening and speaking to students from other language backgrounds.

faq.question: Is O.P. Jindal Global University public or private?
faq.answer: It is private. The University Grants Commission lists O.P. Jindal Global University, Sonipat among the private universities of Haryana, established under the Haryana Private Universities Act, 2006 by a notification dated 10 November 2006, and founded in 2009 as a non-profit philanthropic initiative. The UGC also notified it as an Institution of Eminence on 4 November 2020, one of only four private institutions on that twelve-strong national list.

faq.question: What language are the programmes taught in?
faq.answer: English. The JGU Academic Regulations state that the medium of instruction and assessment at the university is English unless the Academic Council determines otherwise for a specific course or programme. There is no local-language teaching phase in the liberal arts, political science, public policy, public health or MBA programmes listed here.

faq.question: Do international students pay a different fee?
faq.answer: No. JGU publishes one fee schedule and applies it to Indian, NRI and international students alike, and states that it has no NRI or Foreign National quota, no management quota and no donation or capitation seats. Admission is on merit through the same rounds every applicant goes through.

faq.question: What does a year actually cost?
faq.answer: For 2026-27, tuition ranges from INR 3,50,000 for the B.A. (Hons.) Political Science to INR 7,00,000 for the Full-Time MBA and the five-year law degrees. Residential programmes add INR 2,32,000, INR 2,31,100 or INR 1,81,100 a year in residential charges, plus INR 1,48,900 on the law degrees or INR 1,24,900 elsewhere in allied services covering food, laundry, security, housekeeping and electricity. A one-time refundable deposit of INR 50,000 applies. The Master of Public Health is non-residential and costs INR 3,50,000 plus the deposit.

faq.question: Do the fees increase during the degree?
faq.answer: Yes. JGU states that tuition, residential and allied service charges are each subject to an annual increase of up to ten per cent. On a four-year undergraduate degree that compounding makes the final year noticeably more expensive than the first, so the total cost of the degree is higher than four times the first-year figure.

faq.question: How do I apply, and through which portal?
faq.answer: Applications go through admissions.jgu.edu.in, JGU's own admissions portal, and JGU states that it does not appoint or authorise any agent, intermediary or consultant for admissions. Undergraduate applicants submit a personal statement and supplemental questions, sit the JSAT or an accepted equivalent, and attend an online faculty interview.

faq.question: What entrance test do I need?
faq.answer: It depends on the programme. Liberal arts and political science applicants need a JSAT score or an at-par SAT or ACT result. The five-year law degrees are decided on the LNAT-UK, and Jindal Global Law School states it accepts no other law admissions test. The Full-Time MBA requires GMAT 450 or above, GRE 295 or above, NMAT 160 or above, or CAT, MAT, XAT, CMAT or ATMA at the 50th percentile or above, for the 2026 admission cycle. The M.A. Public Policy uses its own closed-book examination, and the MPH an online entrance test or a listed national or international test score.

faq.question: Is an English-language test required?
faq.answer: The published eligibility criteria for the liberal arts, political science, public policy, public health and MBA programmes do not list an IELTS or TOEFL requirement. JGU runs an English Language Centre, established in 2012, that supports students from other language backgrounds across reading, writing, listening and speaking once they are enrolled.

faq.question: What do I need if my degree was awarded outside India?
faq.answer: Postgraduate applicants holding a bachelor's degree from outside India must submit an equivalency certificate from the Association of Indian Universities. Undergraduate applicants schooled outside India must have completed twelve years of education recognised in their own country, with a grading conversion sheet or normalisation scale where the board does not use Indian grading. JGU accepts IB Diploma and IB Career-related Programme candidates only, not IB Certificate holders, and Cambridge applicants need a minimum of 24 credits.

faq.question: What recognition does JGU hold, and what does it mean for me?
faq.answer: Three things carry weight. The UGC lists JGU among Haryana's private universities under the Haryana Private Universities Act, 2006, so its degrees are UGC-recognised. The UGC separately notified JGU as an Institution of Eminence on 4 November 2020. And the Bar Council of India records Jindal Global Law School on its approved list of Centres of Legal Education, approved to 2026-27, which is what makes the five-year law degrees valid Indian law qualifications. BCI approval governs India; whether any degree opens professional practice elsewhere is decided by that jurisdiction's own regulator. JGU holds no current NAAC accreditation.

faq.question: When do classes start and is there more than one intake?
faq.answer: There is one annual entry point for these programmes. The JGU Academic Calendar 2026-2027 begins Fall Semester A classes on 3 August 2026 across all schools, and sets Term 1 of the one-year master's structure from the same date. The Master of Public Health runs on its own schedule, with Term 1 from 4 September 2026 to 25 October 2026.

faq.question: What visa and registration steps apply after admission?
faq.answer: A study visa is mandatory. JGU states that students travelling on any visa other than a study visa are not eligible to study or register, that the visa must name O.P. Jindal Global University, and that it must be valid from programme registration until after the study end date. Processing can take three months or longer. After arrival, e-FRRO registration must be completed within 14 days, using a bonafide letter and residence proof issued by the international office and collected within three days of reaching campus.

faq.question: What accommodation will I get?
faq.answer: Shared rooms. The Student Handbook states that JGU accommodation is on a three- and four-people sharing basis with no single occupancy available, in separate blocks for male and female students. Residential and allied service charges are billed annually alongside tuition and cover food, laundry, security, housekeeping and electricity, so most day-to-day living costs sit inside the published fee.

evidence.claimText: Since 2013 Jindal Global Law School has provided the five-year integrated BBA LL.B. (Hons.) programme, which it states adheres to the latest Bar Council of India regulations and University Grants Commission guidelines. Students enrolled from 2025-26 onwards must be awarded no less than 210 credits.
